name: Non-Immigrant B Visa and Work Permit

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a job offer from a Thai-registered company, which sponsors both the Non-B visa and the separate work permit application to the Department of Employment. The company must meet minimum registered-capital requirements (commonly cited around THB 2 million per foreign employee) and, outside BOI-promoted or LTR-exempted arrangements, must generally employ 4 Thai staff for every 1 foreign work-permit holder.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from a Thai company able to meet the capital and Thai-staff-ratio requirements.

requirements.blocker_text: A minimum salary scale applies, tiered by the applicant's nationality (higher for nationals of wealthier countries, lower for others) -- commonly cited in the range of roughly THB 25,000-50,000/month depending on nationality and role.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a salary meeting the applicable nationality-tiered minimum.

evidence_required.document: Employer's work permit application to the Department of Employment
Company registered-capital and Thai-staff-ratio compliance documentation
Degree or qualification documentation matching the role

outcome.duration_length: 1 year, renewable annually tied to the employment contract

sources.title: HelloThailand -- Thailand Long Term Visa Options in 2026, describing the Non-B visa and work permit's employer-sponsorship, capital, and Thai-staff-ratio requirements

STRUCTURAL FINDING: the 4:1 Thai-to-foreign staff ratio is a genuinely distinctive labour-market-protection mechanism, structurally similar in spirit to Turkey's employer-side staff ratio documented elsewhere in this dataset, though the specific ratio and enforcement details differ -- BOI-promoted companies and LTR/SMART-visa arrangements are explicitly exempted from this ratio requirement, a real structural carve-out worth flagging since it means the same underlying employer entity can face very different hiring rules depending on which visa mechanism a given foreign hire uses. pr_after_months and citizenship_after_months use estimated general tracks pending confirmation of the specific years-of-work-permit-held threshold against a primary source; see th_permanent_residence for the employment-category PR track's confirmed 3-year work-permit-plus-1-year-current-employer structure, which this route's holders would typically use.
